# Results — Study 121 (Magic-Formula) on real EDGAR panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Greenblatt's Magic Formula
(ROC + Earnings-Yield combined rank) applied to the S&P 500 survivorship-biased panel
from the desk's shared EDGAR pull. Signal = fundamentals for fiscal year y, predicting
calendar-year y+1 returns (conservative one-year reporting lag). As-of 2026-06-14.*

**Panel**: 233 tickers with all six concepts present for any given year; 2008–2024 forecast
years (fundamentals y → returns y+1 = 2009–2025). **Survivorship-biased** — current S&P 500
projected backwards: all results are upper bounds on any prospective edge.

## The honest test — top decile vs equal-weight market

Signal construction: rank all firms each year by ROC (EBIT / Invested Capital) and EY
(EBIT / book EV = Equity + LTD − Cash); sum the two ranks; top decile = highest combined rank.
Reporting lag: fundamentals from year y used to forecast year y+1 returns only.

| Portfolio | Mean return | Sharpe | HAC *t* | Hit rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Top decile (best MF rank)** | **21.9%/yr** | 1.08 | +5.38 | 89% |
| Equal-weight market (all firms) | 20.7%/yr | 1.51 | +10.51 | — |
| **Top decile EXCESS** | **+1.2%/yr** | 0.12 | **+0.44** | 44% |
| Long-short (top − bottom) | −10.6%/yr | −0.35 | **−1.43** | 39% |

- The top decile earns **+1.2%/yr** above the equal-weight market, HAC *t* = **+0.44** —
  statistically **indistinguishable from zero** on 17 annual observations.
- The **long-short hedge inverts**: the bottom decile (lowest combined rank) outperforms
  the top decile by ~10.6%/yr, *t* = −1.43. This inversion is consistent with the
  small-cap-value literature: on the heavily-analysed S&P 500, quality and cheapness are
  already priced in; the beaten-down cheap/bad-quality names that the formula shorts often
  contain beaten-down cyclicals and special-situations that snap back.
- The top decile beats only **61%** of random portfolios of identical size — barely better
  than chance.
- **Survivorship bias** materially inflates the raw 21.9%/yr headline: a live strategy
  running at the time would have included delisted names excluded from this panel.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Top-decile excess = +1.2%/yr, HAC *t* = +0.44. The long-short
  hedge inverts (−10.6%/yr, *t* = −1.43). On the S&P 500 survivor panel, the Magic
  Formula carries no statistically meaningful directional signal.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No edge to trade: the gross excess is statistically
  indistinguishable from zero, the long-short sign is backwards, and the survivorship
  bias inflates every raw number. Even if the effect were real on small-caps (as
  Greenblatt documented), applying it to large liquid names in a survivor-biased sample
  produces a mirage.
- **Survivorship caveat (upper bound)**: these numbers are from the current S&P 500
  projected backwards. A live strategy running in 2008 would have included companies
  that subsequently failed or were acquired at a discount — the true live excess is
  lower, possibly negative.
